clue.text: Garden reached by way of Kensal Green (Chesterton)

definitions.text: Garden reached by way of Kensal Green (Chesterton)

parts.words: Garden reached by way of Kensal Green (Chesterton)
parts.note: the garden is Eden, and the route comes from the last line of Chesterton's poem The Rolling English Road, where we go there by way of Kensal Green

explanation.surface: Directions to a garden by way of a London district, credited to G. K. Chesterton.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's poem ends 'we shall go to ... by way of Kensal Green'; Kensal Green is a London district with a famous cemetery, so the road leads to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden, the first garden, is the heaven that Chesterton's line says lies beyond the Kensal Green cemetery.

clue.text: Literary club papers

parts.note: Dickens's first novel records the doings of a club named after its founder Samuel, and the book's title calls them its Papers

explanation.surface: The minutes of a book club.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel is The ... Papers, the posthumous record of the club founded by Samuel of that surname.

clue.text: Holding back all those left outside school

indicators.note: outside says the word for those left wraps round the word for school

parts.note: the rest are all those who remain
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Everyone left outside the school gates is being kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun, a place of learning, but here it is the verb meaning to drill or coach; 'outside' splits the leftovers word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back one's feelings or actions is showing self-control, a synonym.

clue.text: Watches their faces

parts.note: read as the faces belonging to watches, the numbered plates that show the time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on people's faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a verb, someone watching faces; it is the noun, timepieces, whose faces are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked face of a clock or watch, where the hands point to the hours, is its name.

clue.text: Where the jack's self-raising

parts.note: the jack is a ..., who climbs up a church spire, hoisting himself

explanation.surface: Cooking talk about self-raising flour and a jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-raising' suggests flour, but the jack is a steeplejack, a worker who climbs church towers by hauling himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire is where a steeplejack works, climbing by his own efforts.

clue.text: Incident just after a fete opening

indicators.note: after places the word for just behind the earlier letters
the opening of the word fete is its first letter

parts.note: fair means just, even-handed

explanation.surface: Something happened just after a village fete opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as 'only just', but it is FAIR, which comes after A and F (the opening of 'fete').
explanation.definitionFit: An episode or event, as in 'a strange business', is a synonym for an incident.

clue.text: Keeping behind the fans

definitions.meaning: staying at the rear of someone, tailing them
a body of supporters or admirers

explanation.surface: Staying back with the supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping behind is trailing someone; a performer's fans are their devoted supporters, their fan base.

clue.text: A cockfight going at full speed

parts.note: a main is an old word for a cockfighting match

explanation.surface: A cockfight going at a furious pace.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIN is an old term for a cockfight, or a series of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means with full force or at top speed, as of a ship driving on.

clue.text: Broken reel is liable to spring back

indicators.note: broken says the letters of reel and is are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A snapped fishing reel tends to spring back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges REEL and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil or rebound, or to draw back from an agreement, is a formal synonym.

clue.text: Large rainbow over ancient Egypt

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, large
Iris was the goddess of the rainbow, and iris is a word for one

explanation.surface: A huge rainbow arching above the ancient land of the pharaohs.
explanation.walkthrough: The god of the dead and king of the underworld stands for ancient Egypt, his land.
explanation.definitionFit: The god who ruled the dead was the great god-king of Egyptian religion, its chief deity.

clue.text: They click during a dance

parts.note: the shell-shaped wooden clappers held in a Spanish dancer's hands

explanation.surface: People who hit it off on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'click' suggests people getting on well; it means the literal clicking noise of the Spanish percussion instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco dancers snap these hand-held wooden clappers in rhythm.

clue.text: Pilots may end up in dog-collars

definitions.meaning: guides, shows the way, as a verb
the straps used for walking dogs fasten to their collars

explanation.surface: Airline pilots could end up as vicars wearing dog-collars.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots guide or show the way; dog leashes are clipped to collars at one end.

clue.text: Long-drawn-out communications

parts.note: telegrams, which are made from metal drawn out into long thin strands

explanation.surface: Messages that go on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-drawn-out' suggests tedious messages; metal threads are literally drawn out long, and telegrams sent along them carry the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegrams are called by the name of the cables that carried them.

clue.text: Workers mentioned in the papers on Nelson's Day

indicators.note: the answer is mentioned in, sitting inside, the words that follow

explanation.surface: Staff get a mention in the press on the anniversary of Trafalgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned in' hides the answer in 'paPERS ON NELson's'; Nelson's Day is 21 October, Trafalgar Day, when Britain remembers Admiral Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff, the people employed by an organisation, are its human resources.

clue.text: Female confetti-maker who packed' a punch

definitions.text: Female confetti-maker who packed' a punch

parts.words: Female confetti-maker who packed' a punch
parts.note: a woman bus conductor, who punched holes in tickets and so made little paper discs

explanation.surface: A woman who made confetti and had a mean right hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed a punch' suggests a fighter; the punch is a ticket punch, used by British wartime and later bus conductresses.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a woman bus conductor, from clipping tickets.

clue.text: The House of Bronte for instance

definitions.text: The House of Bronte for instance

parts.words: The House of Bronte for instance
parts.note: the Bronte family lived at the clergyman's house at Haworth, where their father was the incumbent

explanation.surface: The family line of the Brontes as a royal house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House of' suggests a dynasty; it is the actual building, the vicar's home at Haworth in Yorkshire where the Bronte sisters grew up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's official residence, like the Bronte home at Haworth.

clue.text: Change the cane

definitions.meaning: a thin rod or stick used to beat someone

explanation.surface: Reform the use of corporal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To change is to swap; a thin flexible stick for beating is also called one.

clue.text: House aspirant perhaps open to take a brew of tea

parts.note: candid means frank, open

indicators.note: a brew mixes the letters of tea up

explanation.surface: A would-be MP, open to having a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a brew of' rearranges TEA into ATE, which CANDID takes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for the House of Commons is a would-be MP, an example of a contender.

clue.text: Low fellows take half to a place underground

parts.note: base means low, mean
men are fellows

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word to is its first letter

explanation.surface: Base villains taking half the loot to a cellar hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' of 'to' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar or storey below ground level of a building.

clue.text: Stiffener used in making charts

indicators.note: making turns the letters of charts into a new word

explanation.surface: Something to stiffen used in producing charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges CHARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry stiffening, from the carbohydrate used to stiffen collars and shirts.

clue.text: One in fifteen being an angler ?

definitions.meaning: a member of a rugby union team, the forward in the middle of the front row
someone who catches fish with a hook

explanation.surface: A fisherman as one of a group of fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union side is a fifteen, and the front-row forward who hooks the ball back in the scrum has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has fifteen players, one being the front-row player who hooks the ball; and a fisher uses hooks.

clue.text: Battle colour

definitions.meaning: the battle fought in northern Italy in 1859

explanation.surface: Colours of a regiment in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1859 French victory over Austria in Italy, after which a purplish-red dye was named.

clue.text: The month's weather forecast for the London area

parts.note: May is the fifth month
fair is a weather forecast promising good weather

explanation.surface: A monthly weather forecast for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The area is a fashionable district of London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy district in central London's West End, near Hyde Park.

clue.text: Ming vase going, going, gone under this ?

definitions.text: Ming vase going, going, gone under this ?

parts.words: Ming vase going, going, gone under this ?
parts.note: an auctioneer's call before the lot is knocked down with a gavel

explanation.surface: A precious vase being smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going, going, gone' is the auctioneer's patter, and a lot goes 'under' the gavel; the surface suggests the vase being broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The auctioneer's gavel bangs down when a lot is sold.

clue.text: Its houses are in the sky

definitions.text: Its houses are in the sky

parts.words: Its houses are in the sky
parts.note: the zodiac is divided into twelve houses in horoscope casting

explanation.surface: Houses up in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: In horoscope casting the heavens are divided into twelve houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope-casting divides the heavens into twelve 'houses'.

clue.text: A 22-wielder, oddly enough, born to be beat

indicators.note: oddly enough says the letters of the hammer-god's name are put in a strange order

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god, wields a hammer, the answer to 22

explanation.surface: A hammer-wielder born to beat things.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' points to the answer to 22-down, a hammer; Thor wields one. 'oddly enough' rearranges THOR to THRO, then B.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulsate or pound rhythmically, like a heart.

clue.text: Belly noise at the end of the barrel

definitions.meaning: read as bell-y noise, the sound a bell makes
the rim at the end of a cask's staves

explanation.surface: A rumbling stomach at the bottom of a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belly noise' suggests a rumbling stomach, but it is the noise of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell's ringing sound; also a variant of chimb, the projecting rim of a cask.

clue.text: Cuts down on meat

definitions.meaning: fells or hacks, as with an axe
cuts of meat with a rib bone

explanation.surface: Someone reducing the amount of meat they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing or felling is chopping; cuts of pork or lamb with the rib are also called this.

clue.text: Survivor 'of black-out of police transport

indicators.note: out says the word black is removed

parts.note: a Black Maria is a police van for carrying prisoners
the word black itself

explanation.surface: Someone who survived a blackout in a police van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black-out' reads as a power cut; it means 'black' taken out of Black Maria, the old slang for a police van, leaving what survives.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left of the police-van name once its first word is taken away.

clue.text: Softly hold forth after girl is made to disappear

indicators.note: after puts the softly-and-speech pieces behind the girl

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to orate is to hold forth, make a speech

explanation.surface: A girl is silenced after someone speaks quietly and at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Softly' is the musical direction piano, abbreviated in scores; 'girl is made to disappear' reads as a vanishing girl, but the girl only supplies the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that turns to vapour vanishes, so the word means vanish.

clue.text: We hear of one of Pooh's friends in the groove

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spelt as it is said

parts.note: Rabbit is a friend of Winnie-the-Pooh in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: News of one of Winnie-the-Pooh's pals being in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit, of the Pooh books, sounds like the carpentry term.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking term for a step-shaped recess cut along an edge to take another piece.

clue.text: Diana's waxy

parts.note: Diana, Roman goddess of the moon, is shown with a moon shape, and a new moon waxes

explanation.surface: A lady's skin is waxy.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana the moon goddess wears a moon emblem, and the waxing moon has this curved shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved sliver of moon, as when the moon waxes, is the emblem of Diana.
